The three-tier ecosystem formalizes a hierarchical structure where platform (P) enables creator (C) to generate tokens, while end-users (U) engage in peer-to-peer trades. Each tier contributes distinct functional roles: P provides infrastructure, C defines token parameters, U drives liquidity. The token conversion rate is derived from the relationship between reserve and token supply, modeled as a power law. Reserve-based pricing ensures that value accrues dynamically with usage, creating self-reinforcing feedback loops. In GSI, this translates into Bayesian updating of belief states about token utility. In GSE, it maps to state transitions triggered by smart contract execution. The system exhibits duality between supply-side creation and demand-side liquidity, with potential failure modes including reserve depletion or lack of user engagement.
